title: "we will do and we will hear"
hook: "we will do and we will hear" — practice before belief
tomorrow: why they're called words, not commandments

segments.voice: Yesterday: the Exodus, told at the seder as if it happened to you. Your line was we were slaves. Did you do one kind thing for an outsider? Day twelve.

Three months out of Egypt, a crowd of former slaves is camped at the foot of a mountain in the desert. They've been told to wash, to wait, to keep back from the slopes. On the third morning there's thunder, lightning, a thick cloud on the peak, and the sound of a horn getting louder and louder until the whole camp is shaking. Later, the book of the covenant is read out loud to them: what this new life with God will ask. And the people give an answer, all together, that the Talmud would come back to. It's two words in Hebrew, and they're in the wrong order. Today: the mountain, and the answer.
screen: `A MOUNTAIN IN THE DESERT.` → `THUNDER, CLOUD, A HORN.` → `AN ANSWER IN THE WRONG ORDER.`

segments.voice: Sinai is the mountain where, in the Torah's story, God gives the Torah to Israel. Where exactly it stood is uncertain, and the text isn't interested in the map. What matters is what happens there. After the laws are read, in the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation, the people say: "All that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and obey." In Hebrew: na'aseh v'nishma. We will do, and we will hear. Look at the order. The usual order runs the other way: explain it to me first, then I'll decide whether to do it. Here the doing comes first, and the understanding follows. The Talmud tells a story about that moment: when Israel put doing before hearing, a voice from heaven asked, who revealed to my children this secret that the angels use? Teachers hear in it practice before belief. You light the candles before you have a theory of candles. You give the coin before you feel generous, like we saw on day ten. The meaning grows out of the doing. The rabbis also argued about that day, and they wrote the argument down. One teacher said the mountain was held over the people like a barrel, as if they had no real choice. Others answered that they accepted freely, and accepted again in later generations. Both readings are kept. And there's one more teaching: that every Jewish soul, even of people not yet born, stood at Sinai. Converts, too, are said to have been there. The whole people, past and future, at the foot of one mountain. Jews mark that day every year, at the festival of Shavuot.
screen: `THE MOUNTAIN WHERE TORAH IS GIVEN.` · `NA'ASEH V'NISHMA — DO, THEN HEAR.` · `THE SECRET THE ANGELS USE.` · `EVERY SOUL STOOD THERE.` · then, large: `WE WILL DO, AND WE WILL HEAR.`

segments.voice: Forty-five seconds, with the bell. Think of one good thing you've been meaning to do but keep putting off until you understand it better, or feel more ready. A call. An apology. A habit. Picture yourself doing it first, today, and letting the understanding come afterward. The bell holds the time.
Sinai. The mountain of the covenant, where the people answered: we will do, and we will hear. Twelfth word.
Your line: do first. Today, pick one good thing you've been waiting to feel ready for, and do it before you feel ready. Day twelve.

howItsDone: Jews celebrate the giving of the Torah at Sinai on the festival of Shavuot, seven weeks after Passover; some stay up all night studying Torah, and the Ten Commandments are read aloud in synagogue.

original.note: Hebrew: Sinai. the name's origin is uncertain.

trapdoor: what you thought: the mountain where Moses got the Ten Commandments.
what it means: the place where a people answered do, then hear: practice first, understanding after.
what a scholar hears: Exodus 24:7's na'aseh v'nishma, praised in Shabbat 88a, which also records the minority reading of the mountain held over them like a barrel.

sources.quoted: All that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and obey.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 88a (the angels' secret; the mountain like a barrel)
Deuteronomy 29:13–14; Talmud Shevuot 39a (every soul at Sinai)

notes: Editor review 2026-10-01: the hook no longer has the covenant read on the third morning (Exodus 24:7 comes after the Ten Words and the laws); 'most of us would say it the other way' and 'a very Jewish idea' rewritten; 'never stopped talking about' (stock) and 'many' claims softened.
JPS 1917 renders Exodus 24:7 'will we do, and obey'; the script explains the Hebrew literally as 'we will do and we will hear'. Confirm the quoted wording.

Shabbat 88a cited for both the angels' secret and Rav Avdimi's 'mountain like a barrel', with the response of later acceptance (in Esther's time); simplified as 'accepted again in later generations'. Confirm.
The teaching that all souls, including future converts, stood at Sinai (Shevuot 39a and midrash on Deut 29:14): confirm the citation.
'Nobody knows for certain which mountain it was': confirm the phrasing.
